name: Lusca
description: The Lusca is a marine cryptid of Bahamian and Caribbean folklore, said to inhabit the blue holes of Andros Island and surrounding waters. It is most often described as a gigantic octopus or a half-octopus, half-shark or half-dragon hybrid, and is blamed locally for the deaths of swimmers, divers and small craft drawn into blue-hole tidal currents.
full_description: The Lusca is a marine cryptid reported from the Caribbean, primarily around the blue holes of Andros Island in The Bahamas. The name appears to be a clipped form of Mollusca, the phylum of cephalopods, reflecting the creature's tentacled aspect; folklore variously describes it as a gigantic octopus, a giant cuttlefish or a hybrid of octopus and shark, sometimes octopus and dragon. Reported sizes are exaggerated — up to and beyond 23 metres (75 feet) — well exceeding any documented octopus species. The creature's habitat is closely tied to blue holes: vertical underwater sinkholes and cave systems common around Andros (which has more than 170 inland and 50 oceanic blue holes) that are 100–120 metres deep on average and produce powerful tidal currents and whirlpools as the tide changes. Local tradition explains drownings, lost dinghies and missing divers around blue holes as the work of the Lusca. The Canadian wildlife biologist Bruce S. Wright was among the first researchers to document the legend, after a guide on Andros described a 'half-octopus, half-dragon' creature with sucker-tipped tentacles inhabiting limestone caverns beneath an inland blue hole; Wright suggested a giant octopus or rare giant squid. The French cryptozoologist Michel Raynal has proposed that the Lusca might represent an unusually large cirrate octopus, noting a 1984 French submersible (Cyana) record of an undescribed Pacific cirrate octopus measuring about 2.5 m. Television journalist Jeremy Wade investigated the Lusca for River Monsters ('Terror in Paradise', S8E4), concluding that a large octopus is the most plausible candidate behind the legend.
origin: Lusca legends are concentrated on Andros Island, Bahamas, and extend through the Bahamas and the wider Caribbean wherever blue holes and cave systems exist.

etymology.origin: Bahamian English; widely interpreted as a shortened form of Mollusca, the phylum to which octopuses and squids belong.
etymology.first_use: Documented in 20th-century Bahamian oral tradition; brought into English-language cryptozoology in the mid-20th century by Bruce S. Wright.

timeline.event: Bahamian oral tradition of the Lusca is well established and continuously transmitted
timeline.source: Wikipedia, Lusca; PSICAN, Lusca Blue Hole Mystery

timeline.event: The French submersible Cyana films an undescribed Pacific cirrate octopus measuring approximately 2.5 m, providing a real-world reference point for unusually large cirrate octopuses
timeline.significance: Cited by Michel Raynal as relevant to evaluating Lusca size claims

timeline.event: Jeremy Wade investigates the Lusca for River Monsters in the episode 'Terror in Paradise' (Season 8, Episode 4)

cultural_notes: Many Andros residents historically treated the Lusca as a real and dangerous local animal, framing blue-hole drownings and lost boats as Lusca attacks; the belief continues to shape local respect for blue-hole hydrology.
